description: The shape of the whole inventory in ONE call — start here. It answers "what do we own?" (the category tree with an item count on every node, each count covering the node's whole subtree), "how many X do we have?" (find X in that tree and read its count — do NOT page through search_items to count), "what is broken?" (statusCounts per condition: available | in_repair | defect | lost | retired) and "what do I hold?" (assignedToMe plus the first few of those items). Also returns `myPersonId`: the person RECORD behind your login account, which is what "me" means in search_items and assign_item. Every number is org-wide and counts published items only — your own unfinished captures are the separate `draftCount`. Take a categoryId from the tree straight into search_items to see the actual items behind a count.
name: inventory_overview

assignedItems.description: The first few items you hold (use search_items for the rest)

webUrl.description: Link to this item in the web app — give it to your user so they can look at the record themselves. Absent when the deployment has no public address configured

assignedToMe.description: How many items you hold. null when no person is linked

categories.description: The category tree, top level first. This is how you answer "what do we own?" and "how many X?" without paging items

children.description: Sub-categories, same shape (absent when there are none)

count.description: Items in this category AND its whole subtree — the same set search_items returns for this categoryId

draftCount.description: YOUR own unreviewed captures (drafts are personal)

listUrl.description: Link to the full item list in the web app

myPersonId.description: The person record behind YOUR login account — what "me" resolves to in search_items and assign_item. null when no person is linked

statusCounts.description: Item count per condition, keyed by status: available | in_repair | defect | lost | retired. This answers "what's broken?"

title: Inventory overview
